decoder.name: MIT KEMAR 8-virtual-speaker FOA binaural
decoder.note: Headphones recommended. 0° is front, positive azimuth is left, negative is right. This is a fixed first-order binaural preview, not native FOA playback.

cases.title: Solo acoustic guitar, stationary behind the listener
cases.listen: The guitar should sit behind you for the full clip. The late swell near 8s should line up with GT.
cases.request: Compose a spatial audio clip around me with one sources and outdoor acoustics. Place music described as “A solo acoustic guitar plays a gentle, fingerstyle melody. The music has a calm, folk-like quality with a warm and resonant timbre.” in the scene as the first sound. Let it come in near the beginning and finish near the end. Keep it stationary behind me. Use only these sources.

cases.title: Chiptune, a passing train, and a left-side drone
cases.listen: Chiptune stays back-right; the train should travel right to left; the drone stays left.
cases.request: Compose a spatial audio clip around me with three sources and outdoor acoustics. Place music described as “A male vocalist sings in a high-pitched, strained voice over a fast-paced, upbeat chiptune track. The music features synthesized melodies and a driving electronic beat, characteristic of retro video game soundtracks.” in the scene as the first sound. Let it come in near the beginning and finish near the end. Keep it stationary behind me on my right. Place music described as “A train approaches and passes by, its rhythmic clatter and low rumble growing louder before fading into the distance.” in the scene as the second sound. Let it come in near the beginning and finish near the end. Have it move from my right to my left. It should move closer to me as it goes. Place a sound effect described as “A low, sustained, and ominous drone creates a suspenseful atmosphere. The sound is deep and resonant, resembling a synthesized pad or a distant, rumbling engine, building tension.” in the scene as the third sound. Let it come in near the beginning and finish near the end. Keep it stationary on my left. Use only these sources.

cases.title: Three overlapping glitch and noise textures
cases.listen: A left-stationary glitch bed, a left-to-front-right modulator, and a front-to-back receding noise.
cases.request: Compose a spatial audio clip around me with three sources and outdoor acoustics. I want the first sound to contain music described as “A cacophony of distorted, high-pitched electronic sounds rapidly stutters and glitches, creating a harsh, chaotic, and abrasive texture characteristic of experimental noise music.”. It should remain still on my left. Have it begin near the beginning and stop near the end. I want the second sound to contain a sound effect described as “A high-pitched, distorted electronic sound rapidly modulates in pitch, creating a frantic and chaotic effect.”. Have it move from my left to my front right. Have it begin near the beginning and stop near the end. I want the third sound to contain music described as “A cacophony of distorted, high-pitched electronic sounds creates a chaotic and abrasive noise. The harsh, buzzing timbre suggests malfunctioning machinery or a heavily processed synthesizer, resulting in a jarring, industrial soundscape.”. Have it move from in front of me to behind me. It should move farther away from me as it goes. Have it begin near the beginning and stop near the end. Use only these sources.
